mechanism: Map the source cut star-tip (red) and round arc (blue) to BOTH corresponding feature pairs in the two separate openings of A. Unlike the earlier C design, this binds two complete mirrored-looking copies and targets treating a cut meeting the fold as two disconnected holes. Actual fold intersection and all original connectivity remain visible.
mathematical_solution: The source cut intersects the folded boundary at both circular-arc endpoints. Reflection across that boundary makes one connected opening: the two arc halves join in a central circle and the star-like feature is mirrored to both outer sides. D alone has one connected centrally rounded opening with matching left and right tips. A and B have two separate cutouts, E also has two separate openings, and C has only one outer tip and is not symmetric about its fold. Therefore D is unique. Outlining features in A changes no intersection with its fold or number of connected components.
human_gate: Seven 2pt partial contour styles mark a source two-feature pair and its proposed two copy partners in A. No new cut or fold is added. The source still touches the folded edge, both A components are clearly separate, and D remains visible and unmarked.
